scene1_screen1.text: The apartment smells of cardboard, coffee, and new beginnings. The kind that comes with mixed hope and exhaustion. Boxes sit like lazy sentinels, daring her to unpack.

scene1_screen2.text: Ellin sets down a box labeled “IMPORTANT STUFF” and stretches, one hand still cradling a half-finished coffee.

scene1_screen3.text: The ceiling fan creaks. A soft flicker dances through the lightbulb — subtle, like a thought you’re not sure you had.

scene1_screen4.text: (to herself) Well... It's charming if your definition of charm includes squeaky floors and haunted woodwork.

scene1_screen5.text: She walks a lazy circle around the room, kicking a smaller box with her foot as she passes. Sunlight cuts through the window, catching dust in the air — little ghosts in rehearsal.

scene1_screen6.text: (mocking herself) Congratulations, Ellin. You moved into a Pinterest board with abandonment issues!

scene1_screen7.text: She slices open a box and unpacks a chipped mug, a photo frame, and a cracked flower pot—just enough to say, “I live here,” without actually meaning it.

scene1_screen8.text: Out of habit, she checks her phone. 12:12. Her brow furrows.

scene1_screen10.text: She walks to the oven — 12:12. Glances up at the wall clock — 12:12. Opens her laptop — 12:12.

scene1_screen11.text: A chill brushes down her spine. The room hums softly — almost imperceptibly — like it's holding its breath.

scene1_screen12.text: Okay, no way I’ve been unpacking for zero minutes. Unless I fell into a temporal black hole powered by caffeine and denial.

scene1_screen13.text: She steps closer to the wall clock. Her fingers stretch toward the dial, almost touch…

scene1_screen14.text: I wouldn’t do that if I were you. They’ll just go back.

scene1_screen15.text: Ellin spins around. Her coffee nearly flies. Instinct kicks in — she grabs the nearest umbrella like a sword.

scene1_screen16.text: Holy—! Who are you?! How did you get in here?!

scene1_screen17.text: By the bookshelf stands a man. Early 30s. Kind eyes. Worn jeans and a faded shirt. He looks solid — too solid — but the light bends around him like he’s not quite sure how to exist.

scene1_screen18.text: I didn’t break in. Technically, I never left.

scene1_screen19.text: (disbelieving)  Wait, wait. Is this some prank? Are you... an app? Hologram? A really elaborate Airbnb ad?

scene1_screen20.text: (smiles faintly) Nope. Just me. Lari. I used to live here. Then I didn’t. Now I’m kind of... stuck.

scene1_screen21.text: Ellin lowers the umbrella. Just a little.

scene1_screen23.text: As in: “died-here-and-the-building-won’t-let-me-go” stuck. December 12th, 2012. At 12:12. The same minute your clocks seem to love.

scene1_screen24.text: She turns slowly toward the wall clock. Still 12:12. Her phone glows the same. Her breath catches in her throat.

scene1_screen25.text: Are you some kind of ghost?

scene1_screen26.text: (with a small shrug) Feels reductive, but yeah. Let’s go with that.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Hey, look. I’m not here to haunt. You seem cool. Good taste in mugs. I’m just... relieved someone can finally see me.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Nope. You’re special. Congrats. You’ve won the invisible roommate lottery.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen4.text: She doesn’t smile — not yet — but the umbrella doesn’t rise again.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: This isn’t a joke. You should probably ask for a refund and leave.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: This place... clings. Not just to me. To memories. Some people don’t do well here.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen4.text: His voice is calm, but there is a sense of ill will about him.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Let’s skip the icebreaker. Yes, I’m dead. Yes, I’m tied to this place.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen2.text: And no, I don’t know why you’re the one who can see me. But I think you’re part of the reason I’m still here.

scene1_screen27.text: She takes a breath. Long. Measured. The umbrella drops to the floor.

scene1_screen28.text: Fine. I’ll bite. You’re dead, you’re stuck, and I can see you. What now?

scene1_screen29.text: Now? We figure out why you’re the only person who’s seen me in thirteen years. And maybe... why I haven’t moved on.

scene1_screen30.text: Behind them, the old wall clock ticks. Once. Just once.

scene2_screen1.text: Ellin stands frozen in the middle of the room. Her breath comes quickly; her thoughts come quicker.

scene2_screen2.text: (to herself) Okay. Nope. That’s enough. I am done with floating men and haunted clocks. I’m gonna… I’m just gonna lie down for a minute and pretend none of this is happening.

scene2_screen3.text: She grabs her phone on instinct— but her thumb presses 911 before her better judgment can catch up.

scene2_screen5.text: (trying to stay calm) Hi, yeah. Um… There’s someone in my apartment. He says he’s a ghost, but he looks very solid. And calm. And possibly British?

scene2_screen6.text: Are you in any danger, ma’am?

scene2_screen7.text: No. I mean, not unless charming strangers with spectral abilities count? He said he died in here. The clocks are stuck. I think I’m either being haunted or hallucinating.

scene2_screen8.text: Ma’am, have you been under a lot of stress lately?

scene2_screen9.text: I just moved in. Alone. And now I’m talking to a transparent man who knows what time he died. So… yes?

scene2_screen10.text: (lightly amused) Okay. Sounds like you’re overstimulated. Our recommendation? Rest. Hydrate. Maybe skip caffeine after 6 PM.

scene2_screen11.text: The call ends with a soft beep. Ellin stares at the phone. Blinks. Then throws it gently onto the bed.

scene2_screen12.text: Lari reappears — quieter now, almost cautious. He stands by the window this time, looking faintly apologetic.

scene2_screen13.text: I figured they’d say that. I’m sorry. I really did try calling them once, too. But ghosts don’t exactly get callbacks.

scene2_screen14.text: Ellin drops onto the bed and covers her eyes with her forearm.

scene2_screen15.text: I can’t believe I just tried to call 911 for a ghost problem.

scene2_screen16.text: Most people go with sage or exorcisms. You went straight for law enforcement. I kind of respect that.

scene2_screen17.text: She peeks at him from between her fingers. He’s not gloating. If anything, he looks… sad.

scene2_screen18.text: I’m not here to scare you. I don’t know why you can see me. I don’t even know why I’m still here.

scene2_screen19.text: She watches him for a long beat. Her breath starts to slow. The panic settles into something else, something soft.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: I think I’ve finally snapped. I mean, it was bound to happen. Moving alone. Too much caffeine. You’re just… my brain giving up politely.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: If I’m a symptom, I hope I’m at least helpful.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She doesn’t laugh — but the corner of her mouth twitches.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Or — wild theory — you’re not dead. You’re faking. Hidden cameras? TikTok? Is this some ghost-chasing clout farm?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (disappointed, but amused) I died tragically, and you think I’m pulling pranks for internet clout?

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: To be fair, you do have scammer cheekbones.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: He mock-bows. She rolls her eyes — but tension fades just a bit.

scene2_screen20.text: She sighs, pulling her knees up onto the bed, arms wrapped around them.

scene2_screen21.text: I don’t know what’s happening. But if I wake up tomorrow and you’re still here, I’m charging you rent. Ghost or not.

scene2_screen22.text: Deal. But fair warning — I don’t have a bank account anymore.

scene2_screen23.text: Her phone lights up on the armrest. New voicemail.

scene2_screen24.text: "El! Hey! I know you’re still in unpacking hell, but guess what — Harper and I are coming over in three days. Housewarming party time, babe. We’re bringing wine. You bring your cute face. Love you!"

scene2_screen25.text: Ellin stares at the phone like it personally betrayed her.

scene2_screen26.text: Three days. Three days to convince my friends this place isn’t haunted. Great.

scene2_screen28.text: She throws a pillow at him. It passes through. He grins. She groans and flops backward, covering her face with both hands.

scene2_screen29.text: Would you like some help… calming down?

scene2_screen30.text: You’re going to play ghost-therapist now?

scene2_screen31.text: He steps closer — slowly. His hand reaches out and just brushes her arm.

scene2_screen32.text: The moment his fingers graze her skin, the tension in her body loosens — fast. Warmth floods through her, not physical, but deep and full. Her eyelids go heavy.

scene2_screen34.text: Her eyes flutter. Her breathing slows. Besides the fact that Ellin was too exhausted mentally, Larri's touch quickly calmed her down and sent her to sleep.

scene2_screen35.text: Lari stays where he is, near the edge of the bed.He doesn’t speak. He doesn’t move. Just watches her — like she’s something worth guarding. Like he’s afraid the moment will end too soon.

scene2_screen36.text: (to himself, barely audible): I forgot what peace looked like.

scene3_screen1.text: Ellin stretches as if shaking off the weight of a strange dream. She mutters, mostly to herself — part habit, part defense.

scene3_screen2.text: (muttering) Okay. Back to reality. No charming ghosts. No weird clocks. Just coffee and capitalism.

scene3_screen3.text: The kettle hisses quietly. A pan clatters onto the stove. She starts cracking eggs like yesterday never happened.

scene3_screen4.text: Suddenly, the doorbell rings. Ellin freezes mid-reach for a spatula.

scene3_screen5.text: She opens the door to find a tall, spindly man in his seventies. Pressed cardigan, sharp eyes. Alert, suspicious eyes. Neutral expression turned default frown.

scene3_screen9.text: Yes. Ellin Carr. Just moved in. Why?

scene3_screen10.text: There was a boy. Young. Lived here. Then he didn’t.

scene3_screen11.text: Ellin stares. Tries to smile, polite but guarded.

scene3_screen12.text: Well... I’m here now. And unless he left a ghost forwarding address, I think the place is mine.

scene3_screen13.text: Behind her, Lari appears. Calm. Unhurried. Ellin recoils in surprise, but still accepts the fact that Larry's ghost really does exist in her apartment.

scene3_screen15.text: She gestures vaguely in his direction. Mr. Henley doesn’t react. Doesn’t blink. Doesn’t even flinch.

scene3_screen16.text: (confused) You don’t… see him? He’s right here.

scene3_screen17.text: (frowning) Miss, there’s no one there. You may want to get that checked.

scene3_screen18.text: And with that, he turns and walks off, cardigan flapping like a judgmental cape.

scene3_screen19.text: (to herself) Okay... what the hell? He couldn’t see you?

scene3_screen20.text: (gaze lowered) Some people can. Most don’t. It’s not exactly predictable.

scene3_screen22.text: Because not everything wants to be seen. Especially not here.

scene3_screen23.text: Ellin sits cross-legged on the couch with her laptop open. Lari hovers nearby, half-invisible against the bookshelves.

scene3_screen24.text: Alright. You said you don’t remember your death. But what do you remember?

scene3_screen25.text: It was cold. I made tea. Played music. There was this feeling in my chest — like I’d forgotten something important.

scene3_screen26.text: He frowns. Not at her. At the space in front of him — as if trying to see something just beyond reach.

scene3_screen27.text: I stepped into the hallway... And then I was here. Just here. Again. Again. Again.

scene3_screen29.text: The edges are fuzzy. Like someone ripped out the last page.

scene3_screen30.text: She starts typing: Apartment 4B, Brooklyn incident. Brownstone accident. Unsolved 2012.

scene3_screen31.text: Only one result pops up — and it’s vague:

scene3_screen32.text: “INCIDENT REPORTED IN HISTORIC BROWNSTONE. Emergency services were called to the scene following an unexplained disturbance. No further details were made available.”

scene3_screen33.text: “Incident”? That’s it?  No name? No cause of death? No creepy headlines?

scene3_screen34.text: (dry) I guess I died too politely to make the news.

scene3_screen35.text: She shuts the laptop and exhales. Her gaze drifts to the last remaining unopened boxes.

scene3_screen36.text: Fine. I’ll do something normal. Like fight the Box Kingdom.

scene3_screen39.text: True. But if I touch you — carefully — I can lend you energy. It’s like... magical espresso. No jitters, just results.

scene3_screen41.text: (smirking) Only mildly. And I don’t charge for side effects.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: She gives him a long, skeptical look — then slowly nods. He steps closer.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: When his fingers brush her forearm, a soft glow blooms beneath his touch. Not heat. Not cold. Something in between — alive.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Her breath catches. Not from fear — from the ache of remembering what tenderness feels like.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: Her shoulders drop. Her gaze lingers on his face. Her muscles loosen. Her mind clears. She blinks like someone waking up from a fog.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen6.text: That’s… unfair. You calm me down better than sleep or wine.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen7.text: (gentle) Ghost perks. Also, maybe it’s because…you’re the first person who’s looked at me like I’m still real.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen8.text: That catches her off guard. She opens her mouth — but doesn’t speak.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen9.text: She reaches out, fingers grazing his wrist — barely there. The contact deepens the glow, just slightly. Not magic. Not illusion. Something earned.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen10.text: Their eyes meet. The room holds its breath. The moment lingers. And it feels… almost normal.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: Fine. Try it. But if I start levitating or glowing… I’m out.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: She folds her arms — but doesn’t stop him. He brushes his fingers lightly along her wrist.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen3.text: The warmth is instant. Not magical, exactly — just grounding. She exhales — surprised by how much she needed this.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen6.text: He smiles, unsure if it’s a joke or a warning. And for a moment, so is she.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Appreciate the offer, but no ghost boosts today. I like to suffer the old-fashioned way, thanks.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen2.text: Suit yourself. I’ll supervise. Strictly sarcastically.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: She grabs a box. He lounges beside her like a particularly snarky motivational speaker.

scene3_screen42.text: Over the next hour, the apartment starts to shift. Photos appear on shelves. Clothes disappear into closets. The space begins to feel less like a memory and more like a home.

scene3_screen43.text: Still need to grab a few things from my old place. And in a few days… Party time.

scene3_screen44.text: Yes, exactly... Party...People. Wine. Chaos. Human things.

scene3_screen45.text: You’ll need to disappear or play dead. Wait… you’re already ahead of me.

scene3_screen46.text: I can haunt the bathroom. It’s traditional ghost territory.

scene3_screen47.text: She laughs and heads for the door, bag slung over her shoulder.

scene3_screen48.text: (calling back) Don’t spy on me while I’m gone. I’ll know.

scene3_screen49.text: (quietly, to himself) Even if I hide... I don’t think that’ll matter.

scene4_screen1.text: Ellin walks in, phone in one hand, wine bottle in the other. She’s dressed down but glowing. There’s something hopeful in her step.

scene4_screen2.text: (to herself) Alright. Adult party prep, ghost edition. Clean(ish) apartment? Check. Wine? Double check. No visible hauntings? ...Pending.

scene4_screen3.text: She orders pizza with a flourish, sets her phone down, and lights a candle. The room is warm. Inviting. Like it wants to behave tonight. The door bursts open — Nikki and Harper swirl in like glitter-fueled hurricanes.

scene4_screen4.text: Housewarming goddess! We brought snacks, wine, and zero chill.

scene4_screen5.text: Nice place. Smells like sage and mystery. Do I detect secrets?

scene4_screen6.text: (laughing) It’s just lavender incense. But sure, let’s go with “mystery.”

scene4_screen7.text: The evening hums to life: laughter, too-loud music, glitter everywhere. They dance in socks. Share half-mocking, half-sincere toasts.

scene4_screen8.text: But Ellin’s smile sometimes drifts. Her eyes flick, without meaning to, toward the hallway.

scene4_screen9.text: Okay, where’s the bathroom? I’m about to explode.

scene4_screen10.text: End of the hall — on the left.

scene4_screen11.text: Ellin turns back to Nikki — but a scream slices through the music.

scene4_screen12.text: Ellin and Nikki bolt toward the sound. Harper stands frozen in the doorway, pale.

scene4_screen13.text: Inside — Lari. Fully corporeal. Shirt undone, blinking at the sudden company like someone caught in the fridge light at 2am.

scene4_screen15.text: Oh my god, Ellin! Are you hiding men in your bathroom NOW?

scene4_screen16.text: (panicking) No — I mean, yes — I mean, it’s not what it looks like!

scene4_screen17.text: Harper storms back for her bag. Nikki is already halfway out the door.

scene4_screen18.text: We came for wine and gossip, not ghosts in partial undress!

scene4_screen19.text: Good luck, El. Seriously. And maybe... therapy?

scene4_screen20.text: They leave in a flurry of judgment and glitter. The door slams. Silence floods the apartment.

scene4_screen21.text: Ellin collapses onto the bed. Doesn’t cry. Doesn’t scream. Just breathes. Shallow. Furious. Quiet.

scene4_screen23.text: She sits up slowly. He’s not flickering. Not translucent. He looks... real. Alive.

scene4_screen24.text: It’s the full moon. And today is the anniversary. December 12th.

scene4_screen26.text: Until sunrise. The universe gives me one night.

scene4_screen27.text: They sit on opposite sides of the bed — close, but not touching.

scene4_screen28.text: They’re not really my friends. They take, and I let them, because I’m too tired to find better. But they don’t know me. Not really.

scene4_screen29.text: You deserve more than placeholders. You deserve people who see you.

scene4_screen31.text: (with a faint smile) Let me guess. More guests? You’re more popular than my funeral.

scene4_screen32.text: (with a weak laugh) I think you'll like this guest!

scene4_screen33.text: Ellin leaves the room and returns a moment later — with pizza in her hands.

scene4_screen34.text: They sit cross-legged on the bed, pizza between them, sharing slices, sipping wine. Laughter is softer now, slower.

scene4_screen36.text: It’s been years. This is better than crossing over.

scene4_screen37.text: They lean close. Eyes warm. Breath shared. The night deepens.

scene4_choice1.text: How do you show affection tonight?

opts.text: Open your heart. Tell her the truth.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (quietly) I didn’t realize how tired I’ve been. Not just today. Just… all of it.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen2.text: You don’t have to carry it alone. Not tonight.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen3.text: He places his palm gently on her back. Warmth flows into her — emotional, physical, grounding.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen4.text: She breathes in. Shoulders relax. Finally, she lets herself lean into someone.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen1.text: I don’t want this night to pass like the others. Not with you sitting here, looking like everything I never got to hold onto.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen2.text: She looks at him — surprised, but not startled. Like she’s been waiting for him to say it.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen4.text: She nods — just once. He leans in, slow and careful. Their lips meet — warm, steady, no rush.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: The kiss lingers, quiet and full. His hand rests gently against her waist; hers brushes against his chest.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen6.text: When they part, they stay close — forehead to forehead. Breathing the same air. Sharing the same quiet.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen7.text: (whispering) You make me feel like I never left. Like I’m here. With you. For real.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen8.text: He pulls her gently into his arms. She leans into him without hesitation.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Before this ends… There is something I never told anyone. Not in life. Not after.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen3.text: The night I died… I remember thinking I still had time. Time to call someone. Time to fix things. Time to stop feeling like I didn’t matter.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen4.text: She watches him closely now — eyes soft, no trace of pity. Only presence.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen5.text: But time doesn’t always wait. And silence? It follows you deeper than I ever thought it could.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen7.text: He exhales. Something loosens in his chest.

scene4_screen38.text: She falls asleep in his arms. He stays awake a little longer, watching the moon crawl across the ceiling. His eyes begin to fade before hers ever open again.

scene5_screen1.text: Lari’s ghost sits by the front door, distant, quiet. He looks… faded again. Not just translucent. Dimmed.

scene5_screen2.text: Ellin enters slowly, pulling her robe tighter. Her eyes meet his, and neither needs to say what’s changed.

scene5_screen3.text: (gently) You're a ghost again... It's a pity, but also so familiar.

scene5_screen5.text: He rises to his feet, slower now — less substance to carry him. But something is different. Focused.

scene5_screen6.text: Something came back with me. A memory.

scene5_screen8.text: I hid something. In the hallway closet — behind the back panel. I don’t remember doing it, but… I know it’s there.

scene5_screen9.text: Ellin doesn’t question. She moves quickly, almost grateful to be able to do something for Lari. She opens the closet. Carefully removes boxes and coats, then finds a panel. It’s loose.

scene5_screen10.text: Behind it — a small tin container. She opens the lid. Inside: a folded medical report. Yellowed. Fragile.

scene5_screen11.text: (reading aloud)  “Chronic sensitivity to Manganate-7.” Wait. That’s a water treatment chemical…

scene5_screen12.text: Her hands tremble around the paper. This wasn’t just a tragedy — it was negligence. And it cost him everything.

scene5_screen13.text: This was in your system. You were slowly poisoned.

scene5_screen14.text: He doesn’t respond right away. Then — he nods. Slowly. Bitterly.

scene5_screen15.text: I always felt tired. Foggy. The doctors said it was stress. Overwork. But it was this. It was always this.

scene5_screen16.text: (quietly) And no one ever noticed? Why didn't the doctors help you?

scene5_screen17.text: No one asked. No one cared enough to ask. And the doctors needed expensive insurance, which I couldn't afford because of the already expensive rent.

scene5_screen18.text: Ellin grips the paper tightly. Her jaw tightens.

scene5_screen19.text: You didn’t die peacefully in your sleep. You faded, slowly. Because of something preventable. Something hidden.

scene5_screen20.text: Lari sits beside her, though there’s space between their bodies that even grief can’t cross.

scene5_screen21.text: I was invisible before I died. After that... I became just a whisper.

scene5_screen23.text: She looks down at the paper again. At the truth. Cold. Measured. Documented.

scene5_choice1.text: What will you do with Lari’s truth?

opts.text: Tell the world, reveal the truth.
Destroy the document. Give him peace.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: This doesn’t deserve to be buried. You shouldn’t fade in silence, Lari. You should be heard. Even now.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen2.text: (softly) The world forgot me once. But maybe you’re enough to remind it.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen3.text: She folds the paper with care, placing it into a folder. She won’t shout it from the rooftops. But the story will live — in her words, in her voice.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen4.text: She picks up her phone and makes a note: contact reporters to tell Lari's story.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen5.text: Thank you. I think this is what I needed to move on.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: You’ve suffered enough. You don’t owe anyone your pain. If I let this go… would you rest?

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: (with a nod) Yes. Because you saw me. And that was all I ever needed.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She lights a match. The paper curls and blackens in the sink. Ash flutters, then disappears. So does the weight in his shoulders.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Maybe it’s not for me to decide. But I’ll keep it safe. If someone else comes along... maybe they’ll finish what I can’t.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen2.text: She places the folder back in the tin, reseals it, and hides it behind the panel once more.

scene5_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Even hidden, it matters. Thank you for finding it.

scene5_screen24.text: They sit side by side, not needing words. The air has changed — it no longer holds him captive. It carries him gently, as if the apartment itself is beginning to let go.

scene5_screen25.text: You gave me a voice. You gave me rest. I feel like this will be my last day here.

scene5_screen26.text: (softly) You gave me something to believe in again. And if this is really the last time…

scene5_screen27.text: She turns to him, studying his face as if trying to memorize it.

scene5_screen28.text: (quiet, almost teasing) Do ghosts feel nervous?

scene5_screen29.text: (half-smiling) Only when someone looks at them like that.

scene5_screen30.text: She stands and moves closer. He watches her with reverence, but also… hope.

scene5_screen32.text: She places her hands on his face — and for a moment, he feels solid. Warm. Real. As if, just this once, the apartment grants him weight again.

scene5_screen33.text: She kisses him. Not as a goodbye, but as proof that he mattered.

scene5_screen34.text: His arms fold around her — careful, certain. Like he’s remembering how to hold something precious.

scene5_screen35.text: (whispering into her hair) This… I’ll remember. Even after everything else fades.

scene5_screen37.text: When they part, there’s no sadness in her eyes. Only warmth. And certainty.

scene5_screen38.text: (softly, just above a whisper) Goodbye, Ellin.

scene5_screen39.text: She doesn’t answer right away. Just rests her forehead against his for one last breath.

scene5_screen40.text: For the first time since she moved in, the silence doesn’t feel empty. It feels complete.

scene6_screen1.text: Ellin wakes alone. No ghost in her bed. No warmth beside her. Just the echo of something beautiful that has already passed.

scene6_screen2.text: She moves through the apartment in silence. Grabs a mug, wraps her fingers around it, and closes her eyes.

scene6_screen3.text: All of a sudden, someone starts knocking persistently on the door, ruining her morning intimacy.

scene6_screen4.text: She opens the door to find Mr. Henley standing there again. Same cardigan. Same suspicious frown softened just slightly by the morning.

scene6_screen7.text: The old man nods, but doesn’t leave.

scene6_screen8.text: You know... We never said anything, but he was useful. Mention “weird noises,” maybe a flickering light... and rent gets knocked down a bit. Management doesn’t like bad press.

scene6_screen9.text: (raising an eyebrow) You used a ghost... to get a discount on your rent?

scene6_screen11.text: (after a pause) Don’t worry. I’ll make sure the “ghost” sticks around. Wouldn’t want prices to suddenly spike.

scene6_screen12.text: Appreciate that. We’re all just trying to live here, you know?

scene6_screen13.text: Ellin walks back inside. Closes the door quietly. Just breathe.

scene6_screen14.text: She passes the clock on the wall. It still reads: 12:12.

scene6_screen15.text: She pauses and looks at it. Looks away. Then stops again.

scene6_screen16.text: The big hand moves one tick. 12:13.

scene6_screen17.text: For the first time since she moved in... the clock moves forward.

scene6_screen18.text: (quietly, with a smile) Thank you, Lari. Now it’s my turn.

scene6_screen19.text: She places her mug down. Moves to the window. Sunlight lands on her like a hand — warm and grounding.

scene6_screen20.text: Behind her, the apartment finally breathes with her. Still. But not empty.
